text:
alex: Heads-up: runtime team pushed the "adaptive-window-v1" change to hosted canary (25%) at 1738901234. Early bench shows solid p50/p99 wins and cost reduction. :rocket:

dev-bot: deploy alex/adaptive-window-v1 -> canary (25%) succeeded. see: https://internal.redwood/deploys/1738901234

alex: Quick numbers (canary slice vs baseline): p50 -20% (60ms -> 48ms), p99 -27% (310ms -> 226ms), token cost -11%. Memory use on GPU nodes unchanged.

maria: nice. any regressions on long-seq workloads?

alex: Long sequences (>=2048) show negligible change in p50 and up to +5% p99 due to grouping heuristics; cost still down. We'll add a canary smoke for long-seq.

sam: Product: will customers notice output differences?

alex: No model-level changes. This is serving-layer batching and prefetch tuning. Ran evals, no semantic diffs.

leo: Rollout plan?

alex: Runbook posted. If canary p99 stays good for 24h, we move to 50% -> 100% over 48h. Rollback key: runtime.adaptive_window=false. Command:

```
redwoodctl feature set runtime.adaptive_window=false --scope=hosted --selector=canary
```

maria: thanks. I'll watch my routes and post if any teams want opt-out.

alex: Shoutout to the runtime crew. We'll share a short retro after the 72h window with detailed econ tables. :tada:
